profile.org_note: Single CEO since 2026-01-01: Stuart Miller (Executive Chairman, CEO and President). Under him, COO Jim Parker (East) and EVP Homebuilding David Grove (West) - Area Presidents until 2026-06-05 - oversee eight Regional Presidents listed on the live leadership page under 'Lennar Homebuilding and Land' (Northeast: Mignone; Florida East/North: Gonzalez; Southwest Florida: McMurray; Atlanta/Alabama/Nashville/Gulf Coast: Jensen; Midwest: Burgess; AR/KS/MO/OK: Taylor; AZ/CO/UT: Walker; CA Coastal/Central Valley/San Diego/Las Vegas: Parness), each over Division Presidents who run land buying locally; Texas, the Carolinas, Tampa/Orlando and the Northern California/Pacific Northwest/Idaho/Inland Empire markets have no published regional head. There is no published corporate land chief: per the 10-K corporate handles strategy, land and business acquisitions and financing, land approvals run through the regional and division presidents (several are former VPs of Land), and land-bank/capital structuring sits with CFO Diane Bessette, Treasurer Lauren Dudley and tax head Michael Petrolino; Greg McGuff, styled Regional President and described in early 2026 as leading 'land banking optimization', the Investor Marketplace and SFR, has been off the leadership page since spring 2026. SEC segments (East, Central, South Central, West) differ from these operating regions.
profile.summary: Delivered 82,583 homes in fiscal 2025 (FYE Nov 30) and was selling in 1,708 communities at year-end, across the 26 states in its 10-K segments plus Delaware, West Virginia and Iowa communities in 2026 releases. The most land-light large builder: about 488,000 homesites owned and controlled at 2026-08-31 with fewer than 2.5% owned; 98% were controlled via options with land banks, land sellers and JVs at FY2025 year-end. Millrose Properties (spun off Feb 2025, externally managed by Kennedy Lewis) is the core land banker and Lennar supplied 88% of Millrose's 2025 option-fee revenue, but the 10-K says Lennar also relies on other land banks for land Millrose cannot acquire, which is the opening for Domain.
